method: Every claim read individually. A claim was treated as misattached only if its text names another event and never mentions Nimitz, Tic Tac, Fravor, Princeton or 2004. Provenance was used to PRIORITISE reading, never to decide: 558 of these claims entered from one record, which tells you they arrived together and nothing about their subject.

1964 Socorro UAP encounter.note: The Socorro event had NO populated node at all - three empty fragments and every claim on Nimitz. Two fragments merged (a45ea4de); the FBI butane-tank report kept separate, since the corpus treats it as a distinct report from the same week.

1948 Roswell UFO incident.note: NOT put on the 1947 node. These claims say 1948 and the digest DECLARES an event node of this name - it was captured rather than created. Filing a 1948 claim on a 1947 node is the exact year conflict the matcher guard exists to prevent.

1950 McMinnville UFO photographs.note: A McMinnville UFO FESTIVAL node exists and would have been the wrong home. The claims are about Paul Trent's 1950 photographs.

Roswell UFO Festival.note: Same trap the other way: two claims about the annual festival, not the 1947 incident.

Kenneth Arnold Unidentified Flying Objec.note: f14cba03 names Roswell only as a time reference - 'a couple of weeks before the Roswell crashes'. Its subject is Arnold's sighting.

flagged_for_you.text: Chris Ramsey states that the Roswell crash and the sighting by Kenneth Arnold, followed by the Aztec crash, prompted government and military interest in UFOs, leading to the formation of Project Grudge, which later turned into Project Blue Book.
flagged_for_you.why: Names three events and is about none of them - its subject is the formation of Project Grudge. Assigning it to any one event would be a guess, so it is LEFT on the Nimitz node, wrong but visible, rather than moved to a plausible home.

integrity.the_one_reduction: a claim that already referenced its destination; the duplicate collapsed rather than a reference being lost

second_pass.claim_node_refs: 65353 before and after - a clean move, nothing dropped

not_done.why: 851 claims on this node name neither Nimitz nor another event. Keyword matching cannot settle them and provenance must not: 558 share one source record, and a book about the whole phenomenon discusses Nimitz and a dozen other cases, which is how these arrived. Marked NOT ESTABLISHED rather than resolved by proxy.

second_pass.method: Vocabulary taken from the graph's OWN event node names rather than words I choose, with the year compared - my first version excluded digits and would have absorbed claims saying 1991 into a node named 1973. Clusters were then verified by READING them, not trusted from their label.

clusters_REJECTED_by_reading.Cold War (2): both only mention the Cold War as context - a 1962 Verona sighting, a 1967 Montana posting
clusters_REJECTED_by_reading.Younger Dryas (1): a passing mention inside a belief about Varginha
clusters_REJECTED_by_reading.Dr. X's 1968 French UFO encounter (3): matched on the word 'french' alone; the claims are about the Delphos Kansas ring, a trawler off Urville, and a man outside a gym in Gretz-Armainvilliers

year_conflicts_given_their_own_node.1991 North West Cape UAP sighting: 29 claims say 1990-1991; the existing node is named 1973
year_conflicts_given_their_own_node.1980 Texas diamond-shaped UAP encounter: 8 claims describe a December 1980 encounter; the node is named 1950 Del Rio
year_conflicts_given_their_own_node.1952 Los Alamos National Laboratory UAP: 2 claims say July 1952; the node is named 1950

NOT_ESTABLISHED.WARNING: The Nimitz node holds 1,035 refs of which only 405 mention Nimitz, Tic Tac, Fravor, Princeton or 2004. THE REMAINING 630 ARE UNVERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED-CORRECT. A reader finding a tidier node should not read that as a clean bill: 135 name more than one event and are ambiguous, 489 name no event at all, and 6 were clustered but rejected on reading.
NOT_ESTABLISHED.why_not_resolved: Keyword matching cannot settle them and provenance must not: 558 share one source record, and a book about the whole phenomenon discusses Nimitz alongside a dozen other cases, which is how they arrived here. Resolving them by proxy would be the original mechanism with better manners.
